questions.question: What are the three parts of an effective presentation structure?
questions.explanation: Effective presentations follow a clear introduction-body-conclusion structure that helps both speaker and audience stay oriented.

questions.question: What is the 6-by-6 rule for presentation slides?
options: No more than 6 bullet points per slide and 6 words per bullet
questions.explanation: The 6-by-6 rule keeps slides readable: at most six bullet points per slide and about six words per bullet, so the audience listens to you rather than reading.

questions.question: What is the proper role of visual aids in a presentation?
options: To support your message, not replace it
questions.explanation: Slides and visuals should reinforce what you say; the audience should be listening to you, not reading dense text.

questions.question: Which delivery technique improves audience engagement?
options: Varying your pace and using deliberate pauses
Reading every word from the slides
questions.explanation: Varied pace, strategic pauses, eye contact, and confident posture keep audiences engaged and help them retain your message.

questions.question: What should the introduction of a presentation accomplish?
options: Capture attention, establish the topic, and preview the structure
questions.explanation: A strong introduction hooks the audience, makes the topic and purpose clear, and gives a roadmap of what is coming.
